inputs: options-flow-feed-lab.lean=call-heavy (leaning bullish); tickers=12; contractsFlagged=1798; callFraction=0.7091; topPrint=AMD 470C $7.1M on 9.2x OI
items.method: Compare current daily breadth versus the 60% broad-participation threshold against the prior window's breadth to detect a participation shift, then test whether the option-flow premium lean and the size of its most-unusual single print confirm or contradict that shift, and overlay the VIX band and the benchmark moving-average stack to judge whether call-heavy premium is now leaning into a broadening tape rather than a narrow one.
items.note: The genuinely new feature this window is a breadth heal: daily participation has jumped to 56.52% of the 134 market-heatmap constituents from about 29.99% into the prior close, cutting the shortfall to the 60% broad-participation line to just 3.48 points from roughly 30, while option premium stays call-heavy — 1798 contracts clear the $250k bar inside 30 days at a 0.71 call fraction — and the single most-unusual print has cooled to an AMD 470 call at $7.1M on 9.2x its open interest from the prior window's nine-figure TSLA 360 call. VIX has eased to 15.13 and SPY is bull-stacked just 1.56% under its 52-week high. So the persistent upside premium is now leaning into a broadening tape rather than the narrow one flagged at the prior close, though breadth still sits under the 60% line. Watch for breadth to clear the 60% line to confirm the broadening; the constructive read is invalidated on a daily close below 760.00 on SPY, which would reopen the narrow-participation risk.
items.title: SPY daily breadth healed to 56.52% from about 30% into the prior close while call premium stayed heavy at 1798 flagged contracts — persistent upside premium now leaning into a broadening tape rather than a narrow one

inputs: options-structure-lab.regime=negative dealer gamma; flip=769.59; callWall=766; putWall=765; expectedMove=2.67; spot=765.72
items.method: Read the options-structure gamma sign, flip and wall levels against current benchmark spot, compare the flip-versus-spot gap and the expected-move width to the prior window to detect whether the flip has migrated away from spot and the corridor has compressed, confirm the dealer scenario and conviction from the gamma playbook, then overlay the intraday session type and VWAP and the VIX band, to judge whether a spot pinned well below a lifted flip inside a razor corridor is coiling to reclaim or merely pausing before a break.
items.note: The new structural feature this window is a flip that has migrated up and away from spot into a razor-thin corridor: the dealer flip has lifted to 769.59 from 765.59 while the front expected move has compressed to plus or minus 2.67 from plus or minus 3.18, so the modelled range has narrowed to roughly 763.1 to 768.4 with SPY spot 765.72 pinned between the 765 put wall and the 766 call wall and now about 3.9 points under the flip. Signed dealer gamma is still negative, so the level that would turn dealer hedging supportive sits well overhead and the market has to travel to reach it. The gamma playbook still reads range-break-watch with patient conviction, and the intraday auction is a Reversal-risk session with VWAP 765.81 just above spot, while VIX at 15.13 keeps the band calm. This is a tight coil pinned below a lifted flip in short gamma. Watch a clean reclaim above the 769.59 flip as the trigger that relieves the corridor upward, whereas the constructive read is invalidated on a daily close below 760.00 on SPY, which loses the 765 put wall in short gamma and reopens downside toward the lower strikes.
items.title: SPY's dealer flip lifted to 769.59 from 765.59 and the front expected-move band compressed to ±2.67 from ±3.18 with spot pinned near 765.72 about 4 points below the flip — a razor coil under a lifted flip in negative gamma
